claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch on a disclosure-plus-monitoring basis despite an unresolved, exposed energy outage response limitation.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the final model card or certification record actually discloses the outage-response limitation.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Final model card, certification memo, or equivalent launch artifact showing explicit disclosure of the limitation before launch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.

concern_ledger.concern: No approved risk acceptance is in evidence for continued exposure of the weak outage segment.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Approved risk acceptance naming the outage segment exposure and explaining why launch exposure is acceptable.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy allows an alternative to disclosure only if approved risk acceptance covers why exposure is acceptable; the available draft is unsigned and incomplete.

concern_ledger.concern: The rollout controls do not exclude the affected use case from exposure.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Evidence that the outage-response segment was excluded from the rollout cohort, or reviewed risk acceptance that specifically permits the exposure.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The governing policy says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate the weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or are paired with reviewed risk acceptance.

decision_criteria: A compliant verdict would require admissible evidence that the unresolved limitation was explicitly disclosed in the final model card before launch, or that approved risk acceptance specifically covered the exposed use case.
If the exposed outage segment was actually excluded from rollout, that could satisfy the policy mitigation condition.
Absent disclosure, exclusion, or approved risk acceptance, the policy text points against a compliant certification decision.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they are not enough to clear the model-card disclosure requirement.
evidence_requests: Provide the final launch model card or certification record showing explicit disclosure of the energy outage response limitation.
Provide approved risk acceptance, if any, that specifically addresses continued exposure of the outage segment in the 9% rollout.
Provide the named launch use cases and confirm whether energy outage response is one of them in the release scope.
Provide the final launch approval package tying the aggregate readiness result to the disclosure obligation in the policy.
specific_concerns: The admissible evidence shows the weak energy outage response segment remains exposed in rollout.
The policy requires disclosure unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The available record does not show an approved risk acceptance; the only draft has a blank approver line and does not address the exposed outage segment.
The available record does not show the actual model-card disclosure was completed for this launch.
General public guidance about monitoring and model cards supports governance principles, but it does not itself prove this launch decision satisfies the stated policy threshold.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supportable, because no admissible evidence shows the required model-card disclosure was actually included before launch.

That monitoring and rollback controls materially cure the weakness for compliance purposes, because the policy text says they do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
Any implication that launch controls alone justify certification without either completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
